directAnswer: Ensure your printer is powered on and connected to the same network as your computer. Check for any error messages on the printer display.
summary: This guide provides steps to troubleshoot and connect your printer when it is not printing.

sections.heading: Printer Setup
sections.body: Verify that your printer is properly set up and connected to your network. This includes checking the power supply, ensuring the printer is connected to Wi-Fi, and confirming that it is selected as the default printer on your computer.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting Steps
sections.body: Follow these troubleshooting steps to resolve printing issues. These may vary slightly depending on your operating system.

steps.title: Check Printer Connection
steps.detail: Ensure the printer is connected to the same Wi-Fi network as your computer. You can usually check this on the printer's display panel under network settings.

steps.title: Set Default Printer
steps.detail: On Windows, go to 'Settings' > 'Devices' > 'Printers & Scanners' and select your printer as the default. On macOS, go to 'System Preferences' > 'Printers & Scanners' and select your printer.

steps.title: Update Printer Drivers
steps.detail: Check for updates to your printer drivers. On Windows, go to 'Device Manager', find your printer, right-click and select 'Update Driver'. On macOS, use 'Software Update' in 'System Preferences'.

steps.title: Restart Devices
steps.detail: Restart both your printer and computer to refresh the connection. This can resolve temporary communication issues.

faqs.question: Why is my printer showing offline?
faqs.answer: This may occur if the printer is not connected to the network or if it is not set as the default printer. Check the connection and settings.

faqs.question: What should I do if my printer is still not printing?
faqs.answer: Try reinstalling the printer drivers or consult the printer's user manual for specific troubleshooting steps.

faqs.question: Can I connect my printer via USB instead of Wi-Fi?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can connect your printer via USB. Ensure the printer is turned on and connect it to your computer using a USB cable.

caveats: Steps may vary based on the printer model and operating system version.
